newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Iraq to buy Vietnamese rice over next four years.
newsitem.headline: Iraq to buy Vietnamese rice over next four years.

text.p: Vietnam will continue to supply Iraq with rice as repayment in kind for debt over the next four years, but may agree to exchange petrol products for rice in the future, the state-run Saigon Times Daily said on Wednesday.
The paper quoted visiting Iraqi Trade Minister Mohammed Mehdi Saleh as saying the two countries could exchange food for oil once the United Nations embargo on Iraq was eased.
"However, even in the absence of such an agreement, between now and 2000, Vietnam will continue to export rice to Iraq to pay debts to this country," it said.
The debt, the size of which has not been disclosed, stems from aid given by Baghdad to Hanoi during the Vietnam War.
Vietnam has been repaying the debt for years by sending tens of thousands of tonnes of rice annually and Vietnamese workers to Iraq.
Iraq meets most of its needs for rice, estimated at about one million tonnes a year, through imports from either Pakistan, Vietnam or Thailand.
An official at Vietnam's Agriculture Ministry said Saleh's discussions in Hanoi had been general, focusing on the possibility that Vietnam could export rice and tea to Iraq.
However, a Trade Ministry official said Vietnam could take part in an auction organised by the United Nations to sell rice to Iraq. She gave no further details.

Jordanian traders said on Tuesday that Iraq had unfrozen $70 million worth of funds in a deal arranged by an Austrian firm in exchange for commodities purchases. The deal includes supplying Iraq with one 33,000-tonne cargo of Vietnamese rice.
The Saigon Times Daily said the two countries would also hold talks on setting up a joint venture for processing Vietnamese tea, of which Baghdad could buy up to 40,000 tonnes a year.
